name: Statute of Limitations Watchdog

parameters.content:
## Statute of Limitations Watchdog

### How it works

1. Runs once a day. Fetches the firm's user directory, then every open (not-yet-complete) Clio task of a firm-configured type (default 'Statute of Limitations').
2. Computes how many days remain until each task's due date — the actual deadline the firm entered, never calculated or interpreted by this workflow (ABA Op. 512). A matter can have more than one of these tasks (multiple claims, multiple deadlines).
3. Determines an escalation tier: 180 days out, 90 days out, 30 days out, or overdue. The 180/90/30 tiers each alert exactly once (tracked in n8n's own workflow static data, no database) — but the overdue tier alerts on EVERY run for as long as the deadline has passed and the task is still open. Silence about a missed statute of limitations is a far worse risk than a repeated email.
4. Builds an internal alert (color-coded by urgency), addressed to the task's assignee, CC'ing the firm's general alert address once a deadline reaches the 30-day or overdue tier.
5. Logs the alert to the compliance audit sheet, then sends it. This is purely internal — no client is ever contacted, so there is no opt-out gate: a malpractice safety net must never be suppressible.

### Setup steps

- [ ] Configure Clio OAuth2 credentials with task and user-directory read scope (reuse the credential from other templates in this catalog if already deployed).
- [ ] Configure SMTP credentials for sending.
- [ ] Create a Clio task type named exactly 'Statute of Limitations' (or set FIRM_SOL_TASK_TYPE to whatever your firm already uses) — one task per deadline, due on the actual date, assigned to the responsible attorney or paralegal.
- [ ] Set the required n8n Variables: CLIO_BASE_URL, FIRM_NAME, FIRM_EMAIL, FIRM_FROM_EMAIL, GUARDRAIL_WORKFLOW_ID.
- [ ] Activate the workflow. No webhook to wire anywhere.

### Customization

There is no content to customize — every alert is generic, plain-English countdown language with no legal commentary, by design. The only thing firms configure is which Clio task type this watches (FIRM_SOL_TASK_TYPE) and the escalation contact (FIRM_EMAIL).

## Fetch open deadline tasks

Pulls the firm's user directory, then every not-yet-complete Clio task of the configured statute-of-limitations task type, and drops anything without a usable due date.

## Compute urgency and dedupe

Computes days remaining (or overdue) against the firm-entered due date and determines which escalation tier applies, then checks n8n's own static data to decide whether today's tier actually needs a fresh alert.

## Build, log, and send

Builds the urgency-coded internal alert, logs it to the compliance audit sheet, then sends it — no opt-out gate, since this is an internal malpractice safety net, never a client message.

nodes.name: Check Statute Of Limitations Deadlines Daily
nodes.notes: Fires every day at 7am (n8n server timezone) — adjust the cron expression if a different time suits your firm better. Runs well before the business day starts so an overnight-added deadline is caught immediately.

nodes.name: Fetch Firm Users From Clio
nodes.notes:
Fetches the firm's user directory — used by 'Build Statute Of Limitations Alert Email' to resolve the task's assignee id to a real name and email. Requesting 'email' works here because /users.json is the primary resource, not a nested association (Clio rejects a nested User's email — confirmed live in PAC-63).

Runs first in this single linear chain, feeding straight into the deadline-tasks fetch next — a genuine sequential dependency, not a disconnected side-fetch (confirmed live in PAC-63/64 that a disconnected side-fetch referenced only by name in code isn't reliably executed by n8n).

Credential: same Clio OAuth2 credential as PAC-18/20/55/57/58/59/61/63/64/65/66 — reuse it if already deployed.

nodes.name: Fetch Statute Of Limitations Tasks From Clio
nodes.notes:
Fetches every not-yet-complete task, of any type — the next Filter narrows this down to the configured statute-of-limitations task type. Marking the Clio task complete once it's been filed (or is otherwise no longer a live risk) is the entire 'stop alerting' mechanism, same convention as PAC-65's document-request tasks — there's no separate list or field to keep in sync.

The matter's display_number/description come along nested one level deep on the task itself (matter{id,display_number,description}) — confirmed live convention for tasks.json in this catalog (PAC-59/65) — so no separate matters fetch is needed here; this is purely internal alerting and never needs the client's contact info.

task_type{id,name} and assignee{id,name} as nested fields on tasks.json are each confirmed live individually elsewhere in this catalog but not independently confirmed together with matter{...} in this exact combination — check your first real run's output and adjust field names if Clio rejects any of them.

Credential: same Clio OAuth2 credential as the user directory fetch above.

nodes.name: Split Out Deadline Task Records
nodes.notes: Turns the single API response into one n8n item per task, so the Filter and Code nodes downstream can each operate on individual deadlines. An empty or missing 'data' array (e.g. after a Clio error, or genuinely no open tasks) simply produces zero items.

nodes.name: Filter Statute Of Limitations Tasks With Due Date
nodes.notes: Drops anything that isn't a statute-of-limitations task (ordinary to-dos, deadlines, etc.), or one with no due date set — a deadline task with no date can't be countdown-tracked at all, and that gap itself is worth the firm noticing on its own, outside this workflow.

nodes.name: Compute Escalation Tier And Check If Alert Needed
nodes.notes: Static data is local to this n8n instance's execution store — it won't sync across multiple workers if the instance ever moves to queue mode. Fine for the single-instance deployment this template targets; flag it if the firm later scales to a multi-worker n8n setup.

nodes.name: Filter Deadlines Needing An Alert Today
nodes.notes: Drops any deadline that's more than 180 days out, or already alerted for its current tier today. Everything that survives gets its own alert email — on most days this drops to zero items, which is normal, not a failure.

nodes.name: Build Statute Of Limitations Alert Email
nodes.notes:
Explicitly set to 'Run Once for Each Item' — a real bug found elsewhere in this catalog (PAC-63/65's build-email steps default to 'Run Once for All Items' while only reading the first input item, silently dropping every additional item when more than one qualifies in the same run). Multiple statute-of-limitations deadlines hitting a tier on the same day is entirely plausible and must not be silently dropped.

Color-codes by urgency (amber → orange → red → dark red for overdue) and CC's FIRM_EMAIL once a deadline reaches the 30-day or overdue tier, so it's never just one person's inbox standing between the firm and a missed filing.

nodes.name: Log Alert For Compliance Audit
nodes.notes:
Logs the alert to the OPS1 compliance audit sheet via the Bar-Compliance Guardrail (NTC-33) — internal record-keeping only, not a message to a client. Its 'approved'/opt-out result is deliberately ignored: a malpractice safety net must never be suppressible, same fire-and-forget pattern already used for internal-only notifications in PAC-59/60/61/63.

The guardrail workflow ID is read from the GUARDRAIL_WORKFLOW_ID n8n Variable. This REPLACES $json with the guardrail's own response, so 'Send Statute Of Limitations Alert Email' reaches back to 'Build Statute Of Limitations Alert Email' by name for every field it needs (confirmed pattern from PAC-65/66 — reading $json here would send a blank email).

nodes.name: Send Statute Of Limitations Alert Email
nodes.notes:
Delivers the internal alert to the task's assignee (CC'd to FIRM_EMAIL on urgent tiers). Reads every field explicitly from 'Build Statute Of Limitations Alert Email' by name rather than $json, since the guardrail call immediately upstream replaced the item's json with its own response. An empty 'cc' expression is safe — n8n simply omits the header.

Credential: project → Credentials tab → New → search SMTP → save as 'Email account (SMTP)'.
